regions.name: Central Chile
regions.tagline: Steep High-Andean silt torrents & glacial drainages near the capital
regions.overview: Towering 5,000m Andean peaks frame Santiago's whitewater corridor. Cajón del Maipo and the Aconcagua valley offer powerful, silt-laden glacial volume and steep technical boulder creeks. These are steep, cold, pushy rivers that drop furiously out of the high Cordillera.

regions.name: O'Higgins & Maule
regions.sub: Región VI & VII · Cachapoal, Teno & Radal Siete Tazas
regions.tagline: Basalt volcanic gorges, pristine teacups and deep multi-day wilderness canyons
regions.overview: The transition zone between central arid Chile and lush southern rainforest. The Río Claro de Talca features the legendary '22 Teacups' basalt pool drops, while the Cachapoal, Tinguiririca, and Melado offer roaring canyon runs through rugged wilderness.

regions.name: Biobío & Ñuble
regions.sub: Región VIII & XVI · Alto Bío Bío & San Fabián
regions.tagline: Historical heartland of Chilean big water and granite creeking paradise
regions.overview: The legendary Bío Bío was once revered as the Colorado of South America. While dammed downstream, the Upper Bío Bío (El Nacimiento) remains sacred and magnificent, while the free-flowing Río Ñuble and Queuco provide world-class granite river culture.

regions.name: Araucanía (Pucón)
regions.tagline: The undisputed whitewater capital of South America & PKR home base
regions.overview: Home waters of Pucón Kayak Retreat. With Volcán Villarrica looming above, the Araucanía features the highest concentration of world-class drops, basalt chutes, and clean waterfalls on earth. From the Trancura wave trains to the Palguín drops and Puesco boulder gardens, Pucón is the ultimate kayaker's playground.

regions.name: Los Ríos (Panguipulli)
regions.sub: Región XIV · Fuy, San Pedro, Enco & Seven Lakes
regions.tagline: Crystal turquoise lake outflows, lush rainforest waterfalls and emerald canyons
regions.overview: Directly south of Pucón lies the Seven Lakes district. The Rio Fuy is a global icon: turquoise glacial water pouring over clean volcanic falls and plunging through narrow canyons. Combined with the giant volume of the San Pedro and Enco, this region is pure paddling bliss.

regions.name: Los Lagos & Northern Patagonia
regions.tagline: Grand mountain rivers, granite cathedrals, and the king of big water: the Futaleufú
regions.overview: Stretching from Puerto Varas south down the Carretera Austral into Palena. Here sits the mighty Rio Futaleufú—the greatest continuous Class IV–V big water river on planet earth. Add Cochamó's granite walls, Petrohué's cobalt waves, and the massive wilderness of Puelo and Palena for unmatched expedition whitewater.

regions.name: Aysén & Southern Patagonia
regions.sub: Región XI · Baker, Simpson & Deep Patagonia
regions.tagline: Colossal glacial power, roaring turquoise gorges and raw Patagonian frontier
regions.overview: The deep southern wilderness. The Rio Baker is Chile's largest river by volume: an awe-inspiring torrent of luminous glacial blue water boiling through monster canyons and exploding over El Saltón. Vast, wind-swept, and immensely powerful.

rivers.name: Río Trancura
rivers.section: Upper Trancura (Puente Gary to Curarrehue / Marimán)

optimalFlow.notes: Optimal late spring / early summer flow is 40–60 m³/s. Above 80 m³/s, rapid Marimán becomes a monstrous Class V hole-fest with severe violent eddy lines.

putIn.name: Puente Gary / Curarrehue Access
putIn.accessBeta: Take the International Road east from Pucón past Curarrehue toward Argentina. Turn off at Puente Gary; river access is river-left above the bridge. Respect local Mapuche properties and do not block agricultural gates.

takeOut.name: Puente Marimán or Confluence
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out river-right immediately downstream of Marimán rapid at the raft takeout trail, or continue 3 km to the lower footbridge.

rivers.davidBeta: The Upper Trancura is the proving ground of Pucón whitewater. If you can style the Upper Trancura with composure, you're ready to explore anywhere in Chile. The run starts with pushy Class III-IV read-and-run boulder slaloms through lush Araucanía countryside before locking into deep volcanic basalt canyon walls. The signature drop is Salto Marimán—a thundering Class IV+ to V staircase where water compresses between basalt shelves into a surging diagonal kicker wave and violent hole. Keep your boat speed, charge with aggressive forward momentum, and trust your brace.

keyRapids.name: The Warmup Ledges
keyRapids.description: A series of stair-stepped boulder rapids with broad catching eddies. Great for dialing in edge control and river communication.

keyRapids.name: Canyon Wall Rapid
keyRapids.description: The river constricts against sheer dark volcanic walls. Big compression waves and swirling boils require decisive cross-current ferries.

keyRapids.name: Salto Marimán
keyRapids.description: The crux. Scout river-right. Enter center-right through the tongue, punch the crashing diagonal lateral, and keep hard left boat angle to avoid getting stuffed into the violent boil-hole on the right wall.

hazards: Undercut volcanic shelves on canyon bends
High water creates terminal hydraulic back-washes at Marimán
Occasional strainer trees lodged on gravel bar braids after spring floods
rivers.logistics: Paved international highway CH-199 all the way. 30-minute drive from Pucón town center or PKR. Reliable cellphone coverage at both put-in and take-out.
rivers.pkrProTip: Don't get complacent after Marimán. The boiling eddy lines below the drop have flipped more veteran paddlers than the rapid itself. Maintain active blade pressure until you're completely clear in the slack pool.

rivers.name: Río Trancura
rivers.section: Lower Trancura (Marimán Takeout to Puente Quelhue)

optimalFlow.notes: Always runnable year-round. At 90+ m³/s, the waves turn into giant green surf rollers and fluffy explosive wave trains.

putIn.name: Puente Marimán Lower Access
putIn.accessBeta: Put in below Salto Marimán on river-right where local commercial rafting companies stage.

takeOut.name: Balseadero Quelhue / Puente Quelhue
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out river-left at Puente Quelhue, just 4 km north of downtown Pucón.

rivers.davidBeta: The Lower Trancura is Pucón's community living room. Every kayaker visiting Chile spends afternoons here honing freestyle moves, surfing glassy wave faces, and running guide clinics. It is playful, high-energy, deep-water whitewater with forgiving recovery pools after every rapid. The rapids bear classic names like 'The Junction', 'The Washing Machine', and 'Puente Roto'. Keep your head up for postcard views of snow-capped Volcán Villarrica puffing steam on the horizon as you carve turns downriver.

keyRapids.name: The Junction (Confluencia Liucura)
keyRapids.description: Where the crystal-clear Liucura merges into the Trancura. Big bubbly foam lines, friendly stern squirt seams, and high-energy eddy turns.

keyRapids.name: The Washing Machine (La Lavadora)
keyRapids.description: A ramp of crashing green waves with a powerful surf wave at the top and playful side surfs throughout.

keyRapids.name: Puente Roto
keyRapids.description: Wave train sweeping past old bridge pillars. Clean lines center-left with smooth surf opportunities.

hazards: Commercial raft traffic during summer peak hours (December through February)
Shifting gravel bars and shallow rocks at very low autumn water
rivers.logistics: Super easy logistics. 10 minutes from Pucón town center. Paved road to both put-in and take-out.
rivers.pkrProTip: Bring a half-slice or playboat. The wave on rapid La Lavadora is one of the smoothest front-surf and spin spots in South America when the gauge reads 55 to 70 m³/s.

rivers.name: Río Palguín
rivers.section: Upper Palguín (The Waterfall Run)
rivers.character: Steep Volcanic Bedrock Drops & Iconic Waterfalls

optimalFlow.notes: Small drainage that rises and drops fast after rain. Optimal visual flow is when the rocks at the put-in bridge are submerged but water remains clear.

putIn.name: Termas Palguín Road Bridge
putIn.accessBeta: Drive 7 km east from Pucón, turn onto the road toward Termas Palguín. Follow gravel road 12 km up the canyon to the put-in bridge.

takeOut.name: Lower Palguín Fish Hatchery or Confluence
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the road bridge above the confluence with Río Trancura, or at the commercial trout farm bridge.

rivers.davidBeta: If Chile is the Mecca of steep creeking, Upper Palguín is its temple. First descended in the early 90s, this run became world-famous through whitewater films for clean vertical drops set in lush temperate rainforest. It's steep, technical, and requires precise boat placement. You're boofing over basalt shelves, auto-boofing 15-footers, and negotiating tight slots. You cannot afford sloppy lines here: basalt rock doesn't give, and vertical landings demand disciplined tucks and flat landing technique.

keyRapids.name: Salto de la China (Lookout Only)
keyRapids.description: Massive sheer drop above the standard put-in. Strictly a photo stop; put in below.

keyRapids.name: The Double Drop
keyRapids.description: A 10-foot launch into a turbulent catch basin followed immediately by an 8-foot shelf boof. Timing your second stroke is essential.

keyRapids.name: Tres Huevones
keyRapids.description: Three sequential technical volcanic drops. Must-make boof right on drop two to avoid a pinned pothole.

keyRapids.name: Salto Silenciosa
keyRapids.description: A stunning 22-foot waterfall dropping into a deep, frothing plunge pool. Clean vertical line down the center tongue. Tuck on impact.

hazards: Severe volcanic potholes and siphons along bedrock walls
Wood hazards from fallen Coigüe trees across blind drop entries
High water makes drops violently turbulent with dangerous aerated boil-outs
rivers.logistics: Gravel road, 4x4 recommended after heavy rains. Pay nominal parking fee if parking near private farm cabins.
rivers.pkrProTip: Lock your core and land with a 45-degree angle on Silenciosa. If you land flat from 20+ feet you will compress your lower spine. If you go dead vertical you risk a deep sub-surface hit. Practice your 45-degree landing posture at PKR before dropping Palguín.

rivers.name: Río Puesco
rivers.section: Campamento to Curarrehue Gorge
rivers.character: High-Alpine Boulder Sieve & Continuous Steep Creek

optimalFlow.notes: Snowmelt-fed from the Andean crest near Mamuil Malal pass. Usually peaks November–December.

putIn.name: Puesco Campamento / National Park Guard Station
putIn.accessBeta: Take International Highway CH-199 up toward the Argentine border. Put in near the Conaf / Villarrica National Park entrance station.

takeOut.name: Puente Puesco Lower or Confluence Trancura
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the highway bridge or continue down to the Trancura confluence.

rivers.davidBeta: Puesco is the soul of southern Chilean steep creeking, immortalized by the annual PuescoFest. It flows through ancient Araucaria (monkey puzzle tree) forests under the jagged crests of the Andes. The whitewater is unrelenting: house-sized granite boulders, complex sieves, mandatory boofs, and fast technical micro-eddies. You need an airtight roll, razor-sharp scouting discipline, and an honest crew with solid safety protocols. Every rapid demands respect.

keyRapids.name: The Upper Boulders
keyRapids.description: Warm-up section of steep gradient drops weaving between granite boulders.

keyRapids.name: The Sieve Rapid
keyRapids.description: Scout left. Tight entrance over a bedrock notch into a boiling cauldron. Miss the line and you risk feeding into a sieve pile.

keyRapids.name: Puesco Fest Race Course
keyRapids.description: Continuous, athletic, pulse-pounding whitewater featuring three consecutive boofs with surging compression waves.

hazards: Under-boulder sieves and entrapment pockets
Fast cold water straight from mountain snowpack
Blind drops with minimal bank walking room in the canyon section
rivers.logistics: Paved road follows the river along the valley. Easy visual inspection from the road before putting in.
rivers.pkrProTip: Never paddle Puesco in a group larger than 4-5 boats. Micro-eddies can only hold one or two kayaks at a time. Run leapfrog safety and set throwbags on the crux sieves.

rivers.name: Río Liucura
rivers.section: Magic Canyon (Upper Liucura to San Pedro)

optimalFlow.notes: Fed by pristine spring water and Lago Caburgua seepage. Always emerald clear even when neighboring rivers are blown out from rain.

putIn.name: Puente Liucura / Caburgua Highway
putIn.accessBeta: Take the road north toward Caburgua and turn east onto the gravel road leading to the upper Liucura bridge.

takeOut.name: Puente San Pedro or Confluence Trancura
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out river-right at Puente San Pedro or paddle through to the Trancura confluence.

rivers.davidBeta: The Liucura is pure paddling therapy. You are floating over drinking-water clarity, looking down through 15 feet of sapphire-tinted water at volcanic gravel beds and wild trout. It enters 'Magic Canyon'—a narrow volcanic defile with steep mossy walls where wave trains bounce playfully off bedrock. It's the ultimate intermediate river trip, guide clinic run, and warm-up lap for any paddler adjusting to Chilean currents.

keyRapids.name: Entrance Wave
keyRapids.description: Friendly rolling wave train with easy recovery pool below.

keyRapids.name: Magic Canyon Chute
keyRapids.description: The river constricts into a 15-foot wide basalt slot. Keep straight boat angle through the boil pulses.

keyRapids.name: The S-Turn
keyRapids.description: Fun rapid with swirling pillow waves off the left basalt bluff.

hazards: Overhanging branches and willows in the flatwater braids
Submerged logs after winter storm windfalls
rivers.logistics: Only 15 minutes from downtown Pucón. Excellent takeout parking at Puente San Pedro.
rivers.pkrProTip: Great run for dialed roll practice and bow-stall drills. In high water, the wave in Magic Canyon develops a super glassy dynamic shoulder that surfers love.

rivers.name: Río Maichín
rivers.section: Upper & Lower Canyon

optimalFlow.notes: Tributary to the Trancura near Curarrehue. Runs best in late spring and early summer.

putIn.name: Puente Quiñenahuin
putIn.accessBeta: Take the Curarrehue road and head north along the gravel valley road toward Reigolil. Put in at Puente Quiñenahuin.

takeOut.name: Puente Maichín Confluence
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the confluence bridge near Curarrehue before it empties into the Trancura.

rivers.davidBeta: The Maichín doesn't get the international press of the Palguín or Trancura, but local Pucón kayakers know it as one of the finest Class IV runs in the valley. The canyon is secluded and wild. You drop into continuous boulder gardens, punch through ledge holes, and thread through tight basalt gates. It demands high boat agility and instant reading of downstream horizon lines.

keyRapids.name: Quiñenahuin Drop
keyRapids.description: Right below the put-in bridge. A ramp of turbulent water over slick bedrock shelves.

keyRapids.name: The Gorge S-Bend
keyRapids.description: Steep drop into a compressed canyon corner. Stay off the undercut right wall.

keyRapids.name: The Final Staircase
keyRapids.description: A long, continuous rapid with multiple boof ledges and clean catch-eddies.

hazards: Undercut canyon walls
Steep basalt cliffs make walking out difficult inside the central canyon
rivers.logistics: Gravel road, easily accessible by 2WD in summer. About 45 minutes east of Pucón.
rivers.pkrProTip: Always scout the canyon entrance from the bridge before dropping in to confirm water levels and ensure no fallen trees block the basalt narrows.

rivers.name: Río Nevados
rivers.section: Caburgua Alpine Creek

optimalFlow.notes: Rain and snowmelt reliant. Often runs during spring rain cycles or early snowmelt.

putIn.name: Upper Nevados Bridge
putIn.accessBeta: Head past Lago Caburgua toward Paillaco and up the dirt mountain track.

takeOut.name: Confluence with Río Liucura
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the lower road bridge before the Liucura confluence.

rivers.davidBeta: Nevados is pure high-tempo steep creeking. It drains the high volcanic ridges behind Caburgua into the Liucura. Fast, steep, and cold, it feels like an obstacle course through primeval native forest. You need rapid stroke cadence and quick eyes. If you love classic mountain creeking with clean boofs and zero crowds, Nevados is a hidden gem.

keyRapids.name: First Flight
keyRapids.description: An 8-foot boof launch off a curved rock tongue into a deep green pool.

keyRapids.name: The Slot
keyRapids.description: Narrow volcanic slot with a tricky lead-in eddy. Precise angle required to keep off the rock tooth.

hazards: Wood hazards after spring wind storms
Steep grade means eddies disappear rapidly at higher flows
rivers.logistics: Rough dirt road requires high-clearance vehicle or 4WD.
rivers.pkrProTip: Check with the PKR team before heading up; this drainage flashes quickly after Andean downpours.

rivers.name: Río Turbio
rivers.section: Volcán Villarrica Lava Canyon
rivers.character: Volcanic Basalt Flume & Black Ash Canyon

optimalFlow.notes: Flows directly off the glacier of Volcán Villarrica. Water is silty grey from volcanic ash and glacial pulverization.

rivers.season: November – January (Sunny warm afternoons increase glacial melt)

putIn.name: Volcano Access Road Upper Crossing
putIn.accessBeta: Take the Villarrica Volcano ski access road south from Pucón. Turn off onto the gravel track crossing the Turbio wash.

takeOut.name: Highway CH-199 Bridge
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the main highway bridge between Villarrica and Pucón.

rivers.davidBeta: Nowhere else in the world will you paddle a river quite like the Turbio. The river cuts directly through fresh black volcanic basalt laid down by historical eruptions of Volcán Villarrica. The rock is sharp, dark, and sculptural. Glacial flour tints the water opaque grey. Rapids are fast flumes and punchy drops between black walls. A surreal paddling experience right in the valley.

keyRapids.name: Lava Tube Chute
keyRapids.description: Fast sluice between basalt volcanic walls with vertical compression waves.

keyRapids.name: The Cauldron
keyRapids.description: Steep drop over a volcanic ledge with boiling turbulent water. Scout carefully.

hazards: Extremely abrasive volcanic rock (wear good elbow pads and protect your paddle blades)
Glacial melt causes flow to spike noticeably in mid-afternoon on warm sunny days
rivers.logistics: 10 minutes from Pucón. Fast shuttle turnaround.
rivers.pkrProTip: Start early before afternoon glacier melt elevates turbidity and increases volume beyond comfort levels.

rivers.name: Río Cautín
rivers.section: Malalcahuello to Curacautín

optimalFlow.notes: Optimal in spring and early summer as snow melts from Lonquimay and Tolhuaca volcanoes.

putIn.name: Puente Malalcahuello
putIn.accessBeta: Take Route 181 toward the Lonquimay tunnel. Put in at the bridge near the village of Malalcahuello.

takeOut.name: Puente Curacautín
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the highway bridge entering the town of Curacautín.

rivers.davidBeta: Located north of Pucón in the shadow of Lonquimay volcano, the Cautín is one of the most scenic alpine rivers in Chile. Snow-capped peaks and ancient Araucaria trees line the valley. The whitewater is crisp Class IV boulder slaloms, ledge drops, and fast continuous current. A premier road trip destination when exploring northern Araucanía.

keyRapids.name: The Araucaria Ledges
keyRapids.description: Continuous staircase of boulder drops through stunning monkey puzzle pine forests.

keyRapids.name: Curacautín Canyon
keyRapids.description: Narrow gorge section with big waves and strong eddy fences.

hazards: Cold mountain water; drysuit recommended in October/November
Occasional agricultural fence wires across lower braided reaches
rivers.logistics: Paved highway parallel to the river provides simple shuttle logistics.
rivers.pkrProTip: Combine with a soak at Termas de Malalcahuello or Manzanar after your run for the classic Chilean thermal soak.

rivers.name: Río Malleco
rivers.section: Tolhuaca Foothills to Collipulli

optimalFlow.notes: Best in spring runoff.

putIn.name: Puente Tolhuaca Road
putIn.accessBeta: Access via dirt road from Curacautín heading toward Tolhuaca National Park.

takeOut.name: Puente Malleco Lower
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the road bridge downstream.

rivers.davidBeta: The Malleco cuts through spectacular columnar basalt formations. It features big, dramatic boofs over volcanic ledges and powerful hydraulics. It's a high-commitment run with steep canyon walls where scouting from boat or scrambling over slippery basalt blocks is part of the game.

keyRapids.name: The Amphitheatre
keyRapids.description: Dramatic drop over basalt columns into an enclosed amphitheater pool.

keyRapids.name: The Horseshoe Boof
keyRapids.description: U-shaped ledge drop with a narrow launch tongue on river-left.

hazards: Severe basalt undercuts
Limited canyon egress once committed
rivers.logistics: Remote dirt roads; 4WD vehicle recommended.
rivers.pkrProTip: Bring a breakdown paddle and pin kit; cell service is non-existent inside the canyon.

rivers.name: Río Truful-Truful
rivers.section: Conguillío National Park to Melipeuco

optimalFlow.notes: Spring runoff. Often runs clear out of mountain lakes.

putIn.name: Conguillío Park Road Bridge
putIn.accessBeta: Drive north from Melipeuco toward Parque Nacional Conguillío. Put in below Salto Truful-Truful.

takeOut.name: Puente Melipeuco
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the bridge near the town of Melipeuco.

rivers.davidBeta: Paddling the Truful-Truful is like exploring a prehistoric landscape. Draining the lava dams of Conguillío under Volcán Llaima, this run features brilliant crystalline water crashing through black volcanic stone. Clean, steep boofs, punchy holes, and unmatched natural scenery.

keyRapids.name: Llaima Ledge
keyRapids.description: Steep launch into a boiling aerated basin.

keyRapids.name: The Basalt Maze
keyRapids.description: Technical slalom through maze-like volcanic shelves.

hazards: Sharp volcanic lava rocks
Cold mountain water
rivers.logistics: About 1.5 hours north of Pucón via Cunco and Melipeuco.
rivers.pkrProTip: Take time to hike up and view the main Salto Truful-Truful waterfall in the park before launching.

rivers.name: Río Fuy
rivers.section: Upper Fuy (Lago Pirihueico to Neltume / The Waterfall Section)
rivers.character: Luminous Teal Waterfalls & Tight Volcanic Canyons

optimalFlow.notes: Optimum flows are 20–32 m³/s. At higher flows, the drops become intensely pushy with heavy boiling back-washes.

putIn.name: Lago Pirihueico Outflow / Puerto Fuy
putIn.accessBeta: Put in directly where the river flows out of Lago Pirihueico at Puerto Fuy, 2.5 hours south of Pucón.

takeOut.name: Puente Neltume or Huilo-Huilo Takeout
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out on river-right above the town of Neltume, before the river plunges into Salto Huilo-Huilo.

rivers.davidBeta: The Río Fuy is one of the most aesthetically stunning whitewater runs on the planet. Its water is an unearthly glacial turquoise, warm compared to alpine torrents because it drains the surface of Lago Pirihueico. The Upper section features a series of clean, picture-perfect waterfalls and bedrock slides ranging from 8 to 25 feet. Every drop drops into a deep, forgiving plunge pool. It is the premier stepping stone for paddlers progressing their waterfall boof technique.

keyRapids.name: The Upper Slides
keyRapids.description: Smooth bedrock waterslides with friendly waves.

keyRapids.name: The 12-Foot Boof
keyRapids.description: Clean vertical drop over a curved rock ledge. Plant an aggressive right-blade stroke right on the lip.

keyRapids.name: The 25-Footer
keyRapids.description: Classic vertical drop. Scout river-right. Clean center-left tongue with a deep aerated landing pool. Set safety on the right eddy.

hazards: Must take out before Salto Huilo-Huilo (mandatory egress)
Boiling seams in narrow canyon segments below drops
Higher water makes recirculating hole hydraulics severe
rivers.logistics: Paved road CH-203 from Panguipulli through Neltume. Excellent cabins and camping available in Neltume.
rivers.pkrProTip: Always set safety on the 25-footer and remember: keep your paddle horizontal across your chest and tuck your chin to your deck upon landing to protect your face and back.

rivers.name: Río Fuy
rivers.section: Lower Fuy (Puente Llallanca to Lago Panguipulli)
rivers.character: High-Volume Turquoise Wave Trains & Big Water Boating

optimalFlow.notes: Always runnable throughout the Chilean summer. Fun big water at 50+ m³/s.

putIn.name: Puente Llallanca (below Salto Puma)
putIn.accessBeta: Put in below Salto Puma at the road bridge on the Neltume-Choshuenco road.

takeOut.name: Lago Panguipulli / Choshuenco Beach
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the sandy public beach in the lakeside village of Choshuenco.

rivers.davidBeta: The Lower Fuy is pure unadulterated joy. Gone are the vertical drops of the Upper; here you get rolling, stadium-sized turquoise wave trains and wide, pulsing rapids. It is the perfect run to follow an intense morning on the Upper Fuy or to bring intermediate paddlers to experience big pushy water without consequence.

keyRapids.name: The Entry Rapid
keyRapids.description: Continuous rollers and punchy foam piles.

keyRapids.name: The Canyon Wave
keyRapids.description: Dynamic compression wave flanked by tall temperate forest bluffs.

hazards: Strong whirlpools and boiling eddy fences at high spring levels
Lake paddle out can be windy if afternoon thermal winds pick up
rivers.logistics: Easy shuttle on paved highway. Great craft beer spots in Choshuenco.
rivers.pkrProTip: A great afternoon run. If you take out at the Choshuenco beach, enjoy a fresh empanada and view across the lake toward Mocho-Choshuenco volcano.

rivers.name: Río San Pedro
rivers.section: Lago Riñihue Outflow to Los Lagos
rivers.character: Massive Emerald Big Water & Lush Jungle Canyons

optimalFlow.notes: Drains the entire Seven Lakes chain. Immense, steady volume that runs clean all year.

gaugeInfo.name: Río San Pedro en Desagüe Riñihue (DGA)

putIn.name: Desagüe Lago Riñihue
putIn.accessBeta: Put in on river-left where Lago Riñihue empties into the San Pedro.

takeOut.name: Puente Los Lagos / Malihue
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the bridge near the town of Los Lagos or at intermediate river access points.

rivers.davidBeta: The San Pedro is Chile's grand emerald artery. It takes the combined waters of seven Andean lakes and funnels them through a lush, deep green rainforest canyon. The rapids are wide, grand, and forgiving—huge rolling wave trains, massive friendly eddies, and towering native Ulmo and Nalca plants covering the canyon bluffs. This river was threatened by dams for years and fiercely protected by kayakers and local communities. Running it is a celebration of free-flowing rivers.

keyRapids.name: El Malihue
keyRapids.description: The biggest rapid on the run. A wide staircase of surging green waves and foam piles.

keyRapids.name: The Wall
keyRapids.description: Water pillows powerfully off a mossy basalt wall on the left.

hazards: High-volume boils can spin a boat if edges aren't engaged
Long swim if you come out of your boat in the main canyon
rivers.logistics: Shuttle is longer (approx. 45-60 min). Paved and gravel roads.
rivers.pkrProTip: Pack a drybag with lunch and drinks. There are immaculate white sand beaches along the canyon that make for world-class river picnics.

rivers.name: Río Enco
rivers.section: Lago Panguipulli to Lago Riñihue

optimalFlow.notes: Fed directly from Lago Panguipulli; clean crystal-green water.

putIn.name: Enco Outflow, Lago Panguipulli
putIn.accessBeta: Access via the road from Choshuenco to Enco. Put in at the lake exit.

takeOut.name: Lago Riñihue Inflow (Riñihue East Beach)
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the eastern shore of Lago Riñihue.

rivers.davidBeta: The Enco connects two of Chile's grandest lakes. It is big water, fast, and remarkably scenic. You paddle with views of Volcán Mocho-Choshuenco reflecting off crystalline emerald water. The rapids consist of rapid wave trains and wide sweeping bends. An incredible wilderness connector run.

keyRapids.name: The Chute
keyRapids.description: Narrowing channel with pulsing lateral waves.

hazards: Strong boils on eddy lines
rivers.logistics: Gravel road access; high clearance car recommended.
rivers.pkrProTip: Great paddle to link together with the Lower Fuy for an epic multi-river day.

rivers.name: Río Reyehueico
rivers.section: Liquiñe Geothermal Valley

optimalFlow.notes: Spring runoff and rain-fed.

putIn.name: Termas de Liquiñe Upper Bridge
putIn.accessBeta: Drive from Coñaripe into the hot spring valley of Liquiñe. Put in above town.

takeOut.name: Puente Liquiñe Confluence
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out near the town bridge.

rivers.davidBeta: Deep in thermal country, the Reyehueico drops out of Andean granite ridges through dense Valdivian jungle. Steam literally rises from hot springs alongside the river. The rapids are technical, steep, and continuous with tight boofs and granite slots.

keyRapids.name: The Steamer
keyRapids.description: Steep boulder cascade next to natural thermal vapor vents.

hazards: Tight slots, wood
rivers.logistics: Paved road to Liquiñe.
rivers.pkrProTip: Do not skip soaking in the rustic hot spring pools in Liquiñe right after your run.

rivers.name: Río Gol-Gol
rivers.section: Puyehue Pass to Lago Puyehue

optimalFlow.notes: Spring runoff along Cardenal Samoré Pass.

putIn.name: Puente Gol-Gol / Samoré Pass Road
putIn.accessBeta: Take Route 215 toward the Argentine border. Put in at the road crossing.

takeOut.name: Puente Anticura or Lake Inflow
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out near the Conaf station at Anticura.

rivers.davidBeta: The Gol-Gol is a ferocious, breathtaking volcanic river dropping down from Puyehue volcano. It is famous for legendary waterfalls (including Salto de los Novios) and steep bedrock chutes. It requires precise scouting and seasoned creeking credentials.

keyRapids.name: Salto de los Novios (Scout/Portage)
keyRapids.description: Massive waterfall drop into a turbulent boiling canyon.

keyRapids.name: The Upper Cascades
keyRapids.description: Continuous steep ledges.

hazards: Unrunnable vertical drops
Volcanic undercuts
rivers.logistics: Paved international highway parallel to river.
rivers.pkrProTip: Scout everything from the highway lookouts before dropping in.

rivers.name: Río Futaleufú
rivers.section: Bridge to Bridge (Pasarela Zapata to Puente Futaleufú)
rivers.character: The World's Premier High-Volume Big Water Classic

optimalFlow.notes: At 150–220 m³/s, it is friendly Class IV big water heaven. Above 300 m³/s, waves become towering 15-foot walls and boils demand relentless focus.

putIn.name: Pasarela Zapata Suspension Footbridge
putIn.accessBeta: Take the dirt road 40 km west from Futaleufú town. Park at the suspension footbridge trail. Carry kayaks down to river-left.

takeOut.name: Puente Futaleufú / Macal Access
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out on river-right immediately above or below Puente Futaleufú.

rivers.davidBeta: The Bridge to Bridge section of the Rio Futaleufú is universally acknowledged as the greatest stretch of Class IV big water whitewater on planet earth. The water is crystalline turquoise, fed by pristine Patagonian snowpack and tempered by huge upstream Andean lakes. Everything here is magnified: wave troughs you can lose a truck in, surging boils that spin boats 360 degrees, and exploding pillow waves off granite canyon bluffs. Despite the immense volume, the run is remarkably clean with deep forgiving recovery pools after every drop. It will make you fall in love with kayaking all over again.

keyRapids.name: Entrada (Entry Waves)
keyRapids.description: Towering 10-foot lateral waves that set the tone immediately below the suspension bridge.

keyRapids.name: Cushion (El Almohadón)
keyRapids.description: Massive volume compresses against a sheer granite wall on river-right, generating a 12-foot exploding pillow wave.

keyRapids.name: Mundaca
keyRapids.description: The crown jewel of Bridge to Bridge. A giant stadium-sized rapid with exploding lateral waves and a massive hole at center-left. Line: charge the right-center green tongue with high boat speed.

keyRapids.name: Magic Carpet Wave
keyRapids.description: A world-class glassy surf wave with deep eddy access. Bring your playboat for endless spins and blunt attempts.

hazards: Massive boiling eddy lines that can pull sterns down into vertical mystery moves
Long cold swims if you fail to roll in the turbulence; always stay with your boat
rivers.logistics: Carretera Austral / Ruta 231. 40 km from Futaleufú town. Campgrounds and kayak camps along the corridor.
rivers.pkrProTip: In big water like the Futa, speed is your friend. Don't brake or tentative-paddle into lateral waves—drive your nose forward with confident power strokes and let the hull punch through.

rivers.name: Río Futaleufú
rivers.section: Terminator Section (Puente Futaleufú to Macal)
rivers.character: Monstrous Pushy Big Water & Colossal Holes

optimalFlow.notes: Terminator becomes an absolute monster above 300 m³/s with stadium-sized recirculating features.

putIn.name: Puente Futaleufú
putIn.accessBeta: Put in on river-right below Puente Futaleufú.

takeOut.name: Campamento Macal / Puerto Lorenzo
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at Puerto Lorenzo or continue down to the Macal campground.

rivers.davidBeta: The Terminator section is serious, heart-in-your-throat Class V big water. The rapid 'Terminator' itself is over 1.5 kilometers of continuous, chaotic, thunderous water filled with bus-sized breaking waves, crashing offset rollers, and catastrophic holes. This is not the place for intermediate paddlers. You need bulletproof mental composure, an unconditional roll, and a team running tight visual contact.

keyRapids.name: Terminator
keyRapids.description: Massive 1.5 km long rapid. Enter left-center, weave between enormous exploding pyramid waves, and fight through violent boiling eddy lines.

keyRapids.name: Toro (The Bull)
keyRapids.description: Powerhouse wave train terminating in a heavy crashing lateral.

hazards: Severe multi-minute recirculating holes
Massive boils capable of capsizing even 16-foot rafts
rivers.logistics: Scout river-right along the road high above the river before launching.
rivers.pkrProTip: Have an escape plan and clear signals with your crew. If someone swims in Terminator, your top priority is pushing them into the slack water on river-right before the downstream gorge.

rivers.name: Río Petrohué
rivers.section: Upper Petrohué (Saltos del Petrohué to Ensenada)
rivers.character: Cobalt Glacial Torrent Under Volcán Osorno

optimalFlow.notes: Drains Lago Todos los Santos under the conical peak of Volcán Osorno.

putIn.name: Below Saltos del Petrohué
putIn.accessBeta: Put in below the impassable tourist waterfalls of Saltos del Petrohué in Vicente Pérez Rosales National Park.

takeOut.name: Puente Ensenada or Ralún
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the bridge near Ensenada or paddle through to the Reloncaví Estuary fjord.

rivers.davidBeta: The Petrohué has some of the most vibrant deep cobalt blue water in South America. Flowing out of Lago Todos los Santos under the snow-covered cone of Volcán Osorno, it offers majestic scenery and high-volume Class IV rapids. The riverbed is carved through black basalt volcanic flows.

keyRapids.name: The Osorno Wave
keyRapids.description: Big exploding wave right under the view of the volcano.

keyRapids.name: The S-Bend
keyRapids.description: Sweeping rapid through basalt rock bands.

hazards: Submerged volcanic bedrock ledges
Heavy volume during spring rains
rivers.logistics: Paved road from Puerto Varas (approx. 45 min).
rivers.pkrProTip: Take out at Ralún where the river enters the saltwater fjord: you can paddle from glacial river straight into the Pacific Ocean!

rivers.name: Río Cochamó
rivers.section: La Junta Valley to Cochamó Fjord
rivers.character: Granite Domes & Yosemite of South America Creeking

optimalFlow.notes: Rain and snowmelt reliant. Often paddled as an expedition with packhorses.

putIn.name: La Junta Camp (Hike-in with horses)
putIn.accessBeta: Requires 4-hour hike with packhorses carrying kayaks from the trailhead near Cochamó village up to La Junta valley.

takeOut.name: Cochamó Trailhead Bridge / Fjord
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the trailhead bridge where the valley reaches the sea.

rivers.davidBeta: Cochamó is renowned as the Yosemite of South America for its towering 1,000-meter sheer granite big walls. Paddling out of La Junta is an authentic Andean expedition. The river carves through pure white granite bedrock, polished boulders, and deep clear pools. It's steep, remote, and physically demanding, but the scenery will leave you breathless.

keyRapids.name: Granite Waterslide
keyRapids.description: Smooth granite slide launching into a deep crystal-clear pool.

keyRapids.name: The Cathedral Drop
keyRapids.description: Steep drop beneath 3,000-foot vertical granite walls.

hazards: Extremely remote; evacuation requires horse or helicopter
Fallen logs in narrow slots
rivers.logistics: Arrange packhorses in advance with local arrieros in Cochamó.
rivers.pkrProTip: Spend at least two nights camping in La Junta to hike the granite domes before kayaking down.

rivers.name: Río Puelo
rivers.section: First & Second Canyons (Lago Tagua Tagua to Reloncaví)
rivers.character: Colossal Glacial Emerald Torrent & Remote Fjords

optimalFlow.notes: Massive glacial river draining Argentine lakes into Chilean fjords.

putIn.name: Lago Tagua Tagua Outflow
putIn.accessBeta: Take the ferry across Lago Tagua Tagua and put in at the lake outlet.

takeOut.name: Puente Puelo / Estuario Reloncaví
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the coastal village of Puelo.

rivers.davidBeta: The Puelo is raw, colossal Patagonian scale. You are paddling on emerald green glacial water hundreds of feet wide, bordered by hanging glaciers and sheer rainforest cliffs. The rapids in the canyons feature enormous compression waves, boiling vortexes, and wild wave trains. An expedition-grade river day.

keyRapids.name: The First Canyon
keyRapids.description: Massive surge waves compressing between vertical canyon walls.

hazards: Enormous whirlpools and boils
Cold water
rivers.logistics: Ferry coordination across Lago Tagua Tagua required.
rivers.pkrProTip: Ensure all gear is tightly secured; a swim in the Puelo canyon can mean a 1-kilometer float before reaching an eddy.

rivers.name: Río Espolón
rivers.section: Lago Espolón to Río Futaleufú Confluence

optimalFlow.notes: Lake-fed and crystal clear; great warmup when arriving in Futaleufú.

putIn.name: Lago Espolón Dam / Outflow
putIn.accessBeta: Put in below the small weir at the outflow of Lago Espolón, 6 km from Futaleufú town.

takeOut.name: Futaleufú Confluence Bridge
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the bridge just before it empties into the main Río Futaleufú.

rivers.davidBeta: The Espolón is the perfect palate-cleanser in the Futaleufú valley. While the main Futa is massive and roaring, the Espolón is playful, welcoming, and crystal clear. Fun wave trains, friendly eddies, and gorgeous scenery right outside the town of Futaleufú. Ideal for warmups, playboating, and intermediate progression.

keyRapids.name: The Play Wave
keyRapids.description: Glassy wave ideal for front surfs and spins.

hazards: Overhanging willows on lower flat reaches
rivers.logistics: Only 10 minutes from town.
rivers.pkrProTip: Do this on your first day in Futa to shake off the road dust and stretch your paddling muscles.

rivers.name: Río Palena
rivers.section: Alto Palena to La Junta

optimalFlow.notes: Large multi-day river crossing from the Argentine border down through Northern Patagonia.

putIn.name: Alto Palena Village
putIn.accessBeta: Put in near the border town of Alto Palena.

takeOut.name: Carretera Austral Bridge at La Junta
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the major bridge on the Carretera Austral near La Junta.

rivers.davidBeta: The Palena is the great untamed wilderness river of the south. It flows through untouched Patagonian forests, past pioneer homesteads and snow-capped peaks. Wide, high-volume, and continuous Class III with occasional Class IV wave trains. Perfect for multi-day self-support kayak expeditions.

keyRapids.name: Palena Canyons
keyRapids.description: Continuous rolling waves with sheer wilderness views.

hazards: Remote multi-day environment; carry full repair kit and satellite communicator
rivers.logistics: Long shuttle along the Carretera Austral.
rivers.pkrProTip: Bring camping gear and fish along the way; the brown and rainbow trout fishing on the Palena is legendary.

rivers.name: Río Baker
rivers.section: Upper Baker & El Saltón (Lago General Carrera to Nef)
rivers.character: Chile's Mightiest River by Volume & The King of Blue

optimalFlow.notes: Colossal volume. The Baker drains South America's second-largest lake. The visual sensation of pure cobalt blue power is beyond words.

putIn.name: Puerto Bertrand (Lago General Carrera Outflow)
putIn.accessBeta: Put in right at Puerto Bertrand where the turquoise lake spills out into the Baker.

takeOut.name: Confluencia Río Nef / Carretera Austral Access
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out on river-right above the unrunnable Salto del Nef waterfall, or portage/take out at the highway viewpoint.

rivers.davidBeta: The Río Baker is an emotional, awe-inspiring river. Flowing with a staggering 500 to 1,000 cubic meters per second of luminous neon blue water, it is Chile's largest river by volume. The power is visceral: wave trains that rise like ocean swells, eddy fences that test every ounce of your core stability, and the thunderous rapid 'El Saltón'. Standing on the gravel bar in Puerto Bertrand looking at the Baker will make the hair on your arms stand up. Respect its scale, paddle with power, and savor every stroke.

keyRapids.name: The Bertrand Waves
keyRapids.description: Massive 12-foot rolling green swells immediately below the lake outlet.

keyRapids.name: El Saltón
keyRapids.description: The monster of the Baker. The entire river compresses through a narrow rock canyon, creating a 15-foot diagonal hydraulic and violent boil surges. Scout meticulously from river-right; portage is readily available.

keyRapids.name: Confluencia Nef
keyRapids.description: Where the milky-grey glacial waters of Río Nef slam into the electric blue Baker. Surreal color line and heavy compression boils.

hazards: Colossal whirlpools and boil lines capable of pulling a kayak underwater for several seconds
Mandatory takeout / portage above Salto del Nef (deadly waterfall)
rivers.logistics: Carretera Austral (Ruta 7). Puerto Bertrand has great lodges, cabañas, and local guides.
rivers.pkrProTip: If you portage El Saltón, do it with pride. The Baker is about living to paddle another day. The section from Bertrand down to the Nef confluence without Saltón is one of the most majestic Class IV big water paddles on earth.

rivers.name: Río Baker
rivers.section: Lower Baker (Nef Confluence to Cochrane Bridge)
rivers.character: High-Volume Blue Wave Trains & Vast Patagonian Vistas

optimalFlow.notes: Always high volume and runnable all season long.

putIn.name: Below Salto del Nef
putIn.accessBeta: Hike down the trail below Salto del Nef on river-right.

takeOut.name: Puente Chacabuco or Cochrane Highway Crossing
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the highway bridge connecting to the town of Cochrane.

rivers.davidBeta: The Lower Baker offers all the visual grandeur and rolling swell of the upper river without the extreme Class V crux of El Saltón. You cruise between towering arid steppe hills and snow-draped Patagonian peaks. Big rolling wave trains, wide open lines, and playful eddy surfs.

keyRapids.name: Chacabuco Swells
keyRapids.description: Continuous rollers and big easy waves.

hazards: Strong downstream winds can kick up spray in wide canyon sections
rivers.logistics: Parque Patagonia and Cochrane are nearby for lodging and provisioning.
rivers.pkrProTip: Keep an eye out for Andean condors soaring overhead along the valley cliffs.

rivers.name: Río Simpson
rivers.section: Cajón de Farrellones (Coyhaique Gorge)

optimalFlow.notes: Spring snowmelt and summer rainfall.

putIn.name: Puente Farrellones Upper
putIn.accessBeta: Access from Route 240 connecting Coyhaique to Puerto Chacabuco.

takeOut.name: Puente Simpson Lower
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out along Route 240 before it joins the Mañihuales.

rivers.davidBeta: Just outside Coyhaique, the capital of Aysén, the Río Simpson carves through a dramatic canyon known as Cajón de Farrellones. The whitewater is pushy, fast, and exciting Class IV with steep wave trains, boofs off rock shelves, and vertical canyon scenery. A staple for paddlers making the trek south along the Carretera Austral.

keyRapids.name: The Farrellones Squeeze
keyRapids.description: River constricts through dark basalt walls with surging compression waves.

hazards: Undercut canyon bends
Fast cold current
rivers.logistics: Paved highway parallel to the canyon provides straightforward shuttles.
rivers.pkrProTip: Coyhaique has outstanding local breweries and asados; celebrate your run at one of the craft pubs in town.

rivers.name: Río Figueroa
rivers.section: Lago Rosselot to Río Palena Confluence

optimalFlow.notes: Lake-buffered from Lago Rosselot; reliable flows throughout mid-summer.

putIn.name: Lago Rosselot Outflow / Puyuhuapi
putIn.accessBeta: Access via the gravel road near the village of La Junta toward Lago Rosselot.

takeOut.name: Río Palena Confluence Bridge
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the confluence bridge near La Junta.

rivers.davidBeta: The Figueroa is one of the hidden gems of Northern Aysén. Flowing out of Lago Rosselot with dazzling turquoise clarity, it cuts through ancient temperate rainforest. Continuous Class IV boulder gardens, clean drops, and exhilarating wave trains without the crowds. It's wilderness paddling at its finest.

keyRapids.name: The Gateway
keyRapids.description: First major rapid below the lake with surging waves and deep eddies.

keyRapids.name: The Triple Boof
keyRapids.description: Three sequential ledge drops requiring clean boof strokes on the right.

hazards: Remote canyon; minimal cell service
Occasional wood on gravel braids
rivers.logistics: Gravel road access; high clearance recommended.
rivers.pkrProTip: Combine with a visit to the Queulat Hanging Glacier national park just down the road.

rivers.name: Río Pascua
rivers.section: Lago O'Higgins Outflow to Bajo Pisagua
rivers.character: Extreme Glacial Monster & End of the World Expedition

optimalFlow.notes: Drains the Southern Patagonian Icefield and Lago O'Higgins. Intense glacial power.

putIn.name: Desagüe Lago O'Higgins
putIn.accessBeta: At the very end of the Carretera Austral in Villa O'Higgins. Boat charter required to reach lake outflow.

takeOut.name: Bajo Pisagua / Pacific Ocean Fjord
takeOut.accessBeta: Boat evacuation back through the fjords to Tortel.

rivers.davidBeta: The Pascua is the ultimate frontier. Located at the terminus of the Carretera Austral, it drains the monster Southern Patagonian Icefield. This is serious, high-consequence Class V wilderness whitewater on a massive scale. Only experienced, self-sufficient expedition teams with extensive safety and emergency evacuation plans should attempt this river.

keyRapids.name: The Icefield Surge
keyRapids.description: Massive compression waves through sheer granite walls.

hazards: Complete isolation
Catastrophic volume
Freezing water
rivers.logistics: Requires boat charter logistics at both ends in Villa O'Higgins and Caleta Tortel.
rivers.pkrProTip: Strictly for elite expedition crews. Treat the Pascua with the reverence of a high-altitude Himalayan peak.

rivers.name: Río Bío Bío
rivers.section: El Nacimiento (Lago Galletué to Lonquimay)
rivers.character: The Historic Cradle of Chilean Whitewater

optimalFlow.notes: Drains the pristine high Andes above the dam reservoirs. Free-flowing and sacred.

putIn.name: Lago Galletué Outflow
putIn.accessBeta: Put in where the infant Bío Bío flows out of Lago Galletué in Pehuenche indigenous territory.

takeOut.name: Puente Lonquimay
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out near the town of Lonquimay.

rivers.davidBeta: The Bío Bío is sacred ground in whitewater history. Before dam construction on its lower canyons in the 1990s, it was celebrated alongside the Grand Canyon and Zambezi as one of the world's premier big water rivers. Today, the upper section—El Nacimiento—remains free-flowing, pristine, and wild. You paddle through ancestral Pehuenche territory lined with ancient Araucaria trees. The whitewater is crisp, continuous, and deeply inspiring.

keyRapids.name: Pehuenche Ledges
keyRapids.description: Staircase of clean volcanic ledges with deep recovery pools.

keyRapids.name: The Upper Gorge
keyRapids.description: Continuous boulder slalom with surging wave trains.

hazards: Cold high-Andean water
Respect local indigenous Pehuenche protocols
rivers.logistics: Ruta 181 via Lonquimay. High-clearance vehicle useful for lake access.
rivers.pkrProTip: Show profound respect to local Pehuenche communities along the river; this river is their cultural heart.

rivers.name: Río Ñuble
rivers.section: San Fabián de Alico Canyon
rivers.character: Granite Boulder Gardens & Community Whitewater Pride

optimalFlow.notes: Spring snowmelt (Oct–Dec) brings world-class flows celebrated by the annual ÑubleFest.

putIn.name: El Caracol / Upper Bridge
putIn.accessBeta: Take Route N-31 east from San Fabián de Alico up the valley to El Caracol.

takeOut.name: Puente San Fabián
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the main bridge entering San Fabián de Alico.

rivers.davidBeta: The Río Ñuble is one of Chile's crown jewels of river conservation. Saved from devastating mega-dams through passionate grassroots community activism and the international kayaking community's annual ÑubleFest, the river flows free with spectacular granite boulder rapids. The water is clear, the gradient is steady, and the rapids are athletic, technical, and immensely rewarding.

keyRapids.name: El Caracol
keyRapids.description: Continuous steep boulder slalom weaving through granite blocks.

keyRapids.name: The S-Turn
keyRapids.description: Tight line between granite shelves with explosive lateral waves.

hazards: Sieve pockets among large granite boulders at low water
Fast continuous current at high spring flows
rivers.logistics: Ruta N-31 from San Carlos / Chillán. San Fabián is a welcoming paddling haven with great artisan bread and local fruit.
rivers.pkrProTip: Attend ÑubleFest if your travel dates align in November; it's the warmest, most energetic river festival in Chile.

rivers.name: Río Diguillín
rivers.section: Termas de Chillán Foothills to Recinto

optimalFlow.notes: Optimal during spring melt from Volcán Chillán.

putIn.name: Puente Shangri-La / Las Trancas Road
putIn.accessBeta: Take the road from Chillán toward Termas de Chillán. Turn south toward the Diguillín valley.

takeOut.name: Puente Recinto
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out near the town of Recinto.

rivers.davidBeta: The Diguillín offers steep, technical creeking through magnificent native Roble and Coigüe forests. Fed by the volcanic slopes of Nevados de Chillán, it features clean bedrock ledges, tight chutes, and technical boofing. A top-tier day trip on your way south to Pucón.

keyRapids.name: Shangri-La Boof
keyRapids.description: Clean 6-foot launch off a granite tongue into a foam-filled basin.

hazards: Wood after winter storms
Basalt crevices
rivers.logistics: Paved and gravel roads from Chillán.
rivers.pkrProTip: Combine with skiing or soaking in the hot springs at Termas de Chillán during the spring season.

rivers.name: Río Queuco
rivers.section: Trapa Trapa to Ralco Confluence

optimalFlow.notes: Spring and early summer runoff.

putIn.name: Puente Trapa Trapa
putIn.accessBeta: Take the road from Ralco east along the Queuco valley into indigenous Pehuenche communities.

takeOut.name: Puente Queuco / Ralco
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the confluence bridge near the town of Alto Bío Bío (Ralco).

rivers.davidBeta: The Queuco is a magnificent tributary of the upper Bío Bío basin, flowing through the heart of the Pehuenche indigenous homeland. The river is clear, steep, and sporty with continuous Class IV boulder drops, wave trains, and granite slots. Pristine alpine scenery and rich cultural heritage.

keyRapids.name: Trapa Chute
keyRapids.description: Narrow bedrock slot requiring crisp boat angle.

hazards: Undercut boulders
Cold water
rivers.logistics: Gravel road along the valley; register with local community checkpoints.
rivers.pkrProTip: Be respectful and polite with local community elders; buying local pine nuts (piñones) is customary and delicious.

rivers.name: Río Laja
rivers.section: Laguna del Laja Outflow to Antuco

optimalFlow.notes: Fed by Laguna del Laja beneath Volcán Antuco.

putIn.name: Below Laguna del Laja
putIn.accessBeta: Take Route Q-45 from Los Ángeles through Antuco to Laguna del Laja National Park.

takeOut.name: Puente Antuco
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the road bridge near Antuco.

rivers.davidBeta: Flowing through black lava beds below the active cone of Volcán Antuco, the upper Laja is dramatic and raw. It offers steep ledge drops, violent wave trains, and athletic boofs. The volcanic landscape is severe and beautiful.

keyRapids.name: Antuco Ledges
keyRapids.description: Steep drop over black volcanic basalt shelves.

hazards: Sharp volcanic rocks
Hydro dam releases can fluctuate upstream water levels
rivers.logistics: Paved road from Los Ángeles.
rivers.pkrProTip: Always verify upstream dam release schedules at the Antuco station before launching.

rivers.name: Río Claro de Talca
rivers.section: 22 Teacups (Radal Siete Tazas National Park)
rivers.character: Chile's World-Famous Basalt Teacup Drops & Gorges

optimalFlow.notes: Extremely flow-sensitive. Too low and you will destroy your boat and ankles on shallow pool bottoms; too high and the teacups develop terminal recirculating drowning machines.

putIn.name: Radal Siete Tazas Footbridge
putIn.accessBeta: Drive from Molina into Parque Nacional Radal Siete Tazas. Register with Conaf rangers. Put in below the tourist lookouts.

takeOut.name: Salto de la Leona / Lower Park Boundary
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out before or after the designated gorge exit trail. Steep scramble up out of the canyon.

rivers.davidBeta: The 22 Teacups of the Río Claro is one of the most celebrated and surreal whitewater spectacles on earth. The river has sculpted circular pools—'teacups'—out of polished black basalt. You literally drop 8 to 18 feet from one circular basalt bowl directly into the next. It requires pinpoint precision: miss the boof or pencil in at the wrong angle and you risk fracturing an ankle on shallow bedrock or getting trapped in a churning circular hydraulic. Run it with experienced locals, respect the low flow window, and you will remember it for the rest of your life.

keyRapids.name: The First Teacup
keyRapids.description: A 10-foot vertical drop over a smooth basalt lip into a perfectly circular 20-foot pool.

keyRapids.name: The S-Teacup
keyRapids.description: Double drop with a 90-degree turn inside the bowl. Must-make boof right.

keyRapids.name: Salto de la Leona
keyRapids.description: A sheer 35-foot vertical waterfall dropping into a tight volcanic slot canyon. Scout meticulously from the rim.

hazards: Shallow bedrock pool bottoms (pencil landings can cause serious ankle and spinal impact)
Terminal hydraulic back-washes in the teacups if water is even slightly too high
Vertical canyon walls offer zero escape once committed between drops
rivers.logistics: Paved and gravel road from Molina (1.5 hrs). Conaf park registration mandatory. Bring elbow pads, face guard, and full creeking safety kit.
rivers.pkrProTip: Do not rush this run. Step out on the basalt rim, check the depth of every landing pool with your breakdown paddle, and ensure safety ropes are rigged at the crux drops.

rivers.name: Río Cachapoal
rivers.section: Upper Cachapoal (Sewell / Termas de Cauquenes Gorge)

optimalFlow.notes: Spring and early summer glacial snowmelt.

putIn.name: Termas de Cauquenes Access
putIn.accessBeta: Drive east from Rancagua toward Coya. Put in near the historic hot springs.

takeOut.name: Puente Coya
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the bridge near Coya.

rivers.davidBeta: Flowing down from the towering mining peaks around Sewell, the Upper Cachapoal is a roaring, fast-paced high-altitude Andean river. Grey glacial melt, continuous boulder fields, and big compression waves through a dramatic mountain gorge.

keyRapids.name: Coya Canyon
keyRapids.description: Continuous pushy waves with heavy hydraulics.

hazards: Silt-laden opaque water hides submerged boulders
Mining infrastructure upstream
rivers.logistics: Only 1.5 hours south of Santiago via the Pan-American Highway and Rancagua.
rivers.pkrProTip: Wear warm gear; the glacial runoff off the high peaks is icy cold.

rivers.name: Río Tinguiririca
rivers.section: Termas del Flaco to San Fernando
rivers.character: Steep Glacial Torrent & Dinosaur Track Foothills

optimalFlow.notes: Best in spring runoff.

putIn.name: Termas del Flaco Mountain Road
putIn.accessBeta: Take the mountain road from San Fernando toward Termas del Flaco. Put in where river parallels road.

takeOut.name: Puente Puente Negro
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out near Puente Negro outside San Fernando.

rivers.davidBeta: The Tinguiririca cuts through high Andean badlands famed for fossilized dinosaur footprints. The whitewater is unrelenting, fast, and steep. Big boulder slalom rapids, pushy chutes, and cold mountain volume.

keyRapids.name: The Jurassic Chute
keyRapids.description: Fast sluice between high cliffs.

hazards: Fast current with few recovery pools at high water
rivers.logistics: Gravel mountain road; check road schedule (alternating one-way traffic during tourist season).
rivers.pkrProTip: Check road times before leaving San Fernando as the road to Termas del Flaco often has one-way ascending/descending windows.

rivers.name: Río Melado
rivers.section: Melado Wilderness Canyon

optimalFlow.notes: Spring and early summer expedition flows.

putIn.name: Embalse Melado / Tunnel Outlet
putIn.accessBeta: Access via the historic Melado canal tunnel road high in the Andes east of Linares.

takeOut.name: Confluence with Río Maule
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the confluence with the Maule or paddle out to the highway bridge.

rivers.davidBeta: The Melado is a true Andean epic. Tucked deep in the rugged Cordillera east of Linares, it slices through a vertical wilderness canyon accessible only by kayak. Self-support expedition paddling through continuous Class IV–V boulder rapids, remote riverside bivy camps, and complete Andean isolation.

keyRapids.name: The Melado Gate
keyRapids.description: Sheer canyon entrance with massive boulders and must-make moves.

hazards: Zero road access inside the canyon; self-rescue required
rivers.logistics: Requires full expedition planning and 4WD access to the high tunnel.
rivers.pkrProTip: Pack lightweight titanium gear and freeze-dried meals; keep your boat light to maintain responsiveness in the drops.

rivers.name: Río Achibueno
rivers.section: Montecillo to Linares

optimalFlow.notes: Prismatic crystal clarity; protected Nature Sanctuary.

putIn.name: Montecillo Foothills
putIn.accessBeta: Drive east from Linares along the Achibueno Nature Sanctuary road.

takeOut.name: Puente Achibueno
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the main road bridge outside Linares.

rivers.davidBeta: The Achibueno was declared a Nature Sanctuary to preserve its breathtaking turquoise water and ancient native forests. The paddling is clean, friendly Class III–IV with crystalline pools, playful boulder gardens, and stunning mountain backdrop. An absolute delight.

keyRapids.name: Sanctuary Waves
keyRapids.description: Continuous roller coaster waves over granite gravel.

hazards: Fallen branches along lower braided channels
rivers.logistics: Easy gravel road access from Linares.
rivers.pkrProTip: One of the best camping rivers in central Chile. Pristine campsites on gravel beaches everywhere.

rivers.name: Río Maule
rivers.section: Laguna del Maule to Armerillo

optimalFlow.notes: Spring snowmelt from the massive volcanic caldera of Laguna del Maule.

putIn.name: Below Laguna del Maule Dam / Campanario
putIn.accessBeta: Take International Route CH-115 (Pehuenche Pass). Put in below the dam outflow.

takeOut.name: Puente Armerillo
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the highway bridge in Armerillo.

rivers.davidBeta: The Maule drains an immense volcanic caldera right on the Argentine frontier. Big water, steep volcanic drops, and massive waves compressing between high basalt walls. Powerful and scenic along the Pehuenche Pass corridor.

keyRapids.name: The Campanario Drop
keyRapids.description: Steep drop over basalt boulders.

hazards: Hydro dam release shifts
Cold water
rivers.logistics: Paved international highway CH-115.
rivers.pkrProTip: Check upstream dam operations at Colbún before scheduling your run.

rivers.name: Río Maipo
rivers.section: Cajón del Maipo (San Gabriel to El Melocotón)
rivers.grade: III+ – IV+ (V at high summer melt)
rivers.character: Glacial Big Water Silt Torrent in High Andean Canyon

optimalFlow.notes: At 40–70 m³/s, it is high-energy Class III–IV big water. Above 120 m³/s during hot December afternoons, it becomes a thunderous Class V brown freight train.

putIn.name: Puente San Gabriel
putIn.accessBeta: Take Route G-25 from Santiago up Cajón del Maipo. Put in river-left at Puente San Gabriel.

takeOut.name: El Melocotón / San Alfonso
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the commercial raft landing at El Melocotón or below San Alfonso bridge.

rivers.davidBeta: The Maipo is the lifeblood of Santiago kayaking. Located just an hour's drive from the capital's international airport, it plunges out of 6,000-meter peaks down the dramatic Cajón del Maipo. The water is thick with grey-brown Andean glacial silt, creating heavy, dense waves that pack immense kinetic punch. The rapids are continuous, punchy wave trains, exploding laterals, and fast boil seams. A great place to shake off jet lag when flying into Chile.

keyRapids.name: The San Gabriel Chute
keyRapids.description: Fast opening rapid with towering lateral waves compressing against a gravel bluff.

keyRapids.name: The Roller Coaster
keyRapids.description: Half-mile of continuous, crashing head-high wave trains.

keyRapids.name: The Bridge Drop
keyRapids.description: River pinches through bridge piers with heavy boisterous hydraulics.

hazards: Heavy silt reduces buoyancy slightly and makes water opaque; submerged rocks are invisible
Hot sunny afternoons trigger explosive glacial runoff that can double flow by 4 PM
rivers.logistics: Fully paved road G-25 from Santiago. Fantastic bakeries, empanada stands, and lodges throughout San José de Maipo.
rivers.pkrProTip: Keep your eyes on the daily temperature forecast in Santiago. A hot 35°C day in the city means the Maipo will rise aggressively by mid-afternoon. Paddle in the morning for predictable flows.

rivers.name: Río Yeso
rivers.section: Embalse El Yeso to Maipo Confluence
rivers.character: High-Alpine Boulder Creeking & Glacial Reservoir Outflow

optimalFlow.notes: Controlled by releases from Embalse El Yeso dam reservoir.

putIn.name: Below Embalse El Yeso Dam
putIn.accessBeta: Take the rough dirt mountain road up Cajón del Yeso past the turquoise reservoir.

takeOut.name: Puente San Gabriel (Maipo Confluence)
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the confluence bridge with Río Maipo.

rivers.davidBeta: The Yeso is steep, cold, and alpine. Cutting through stark high-desert Andean peaks beneath Embalse El Yeso, it tumbles down a steep gradient of sharp granite boulders. Technical lines, continuous read-and-run, and breathtaking high-mountain scenery.

keyRapids.name: The Dam Sluice
keyRapids.description: Fast opening rapid on steep gradient.

keyRapids.name: The Boulder Labyrinth
keyRapids.description: Tight slalom weaving through house-sized granite boulders.

hazards: Cold water
Sharp rocks and low air temperatures in early season
rivers.logistics: Gravel mountain road; check municipal road status during rain or snow flurries.
rivers.pkrProTip: Dress warmly; despite warm Santiago weather, Cajón del Yeso sits at over 2,500m elevation.

rivers.name: Río Colorado (Maipo Basin)
rivers.section: Maitenes to Maipo Confluence

optimalFlow.notes: Heavy silt content; fast and pushy.

putIn.name: Puente Los Maitenes
putIn.accessBeta: Turn off G-25 at El Manzano and head north up the Colorado mining road.

takeOut.name: Puente Colorado / Maipo Confluence
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out near the bridge before it joins the Maipo.

rivers.davidBeta: A ferocious mountain torrent draining the glaciated cirque of Tupungato volcano. Extremely fast, continuous current with few catching eddies. Heavy silt and high speed make it a thrilling, high-adrenaline run.

keyRapids.name: The Silt Cannon
keyRapids.description: Continuous steep drop with powerful compression waves.

hazards: Very few eddies; swim would be long and cold
rivers.logistics: Mining road; watch for heavy truck traffic.
rivers.pkrProTip: Ensure your roll is 100% dialed before launching into this high-velocity silt flume.

rivers.name: Río Aconcagua
rivers.section: Salto del Soldado to San Esteban
rivers.character: Legendary Gorge Beneath Mt. Aconcagua & Portillo

optimalFlow.notes: Spring snowmelt draining the slopes of Mt. Aconcagua along the international highway to Mendoza.

putIn.name: Below Salto del Soldado
putIn.accessBeta: Take the international highway Route 60 toward Portillo. Put in below the legendary railroad chasm of Salto del Soldado.

takeOut.name: Chacabuquito Bridge
takeOut.accessBeta: Take out at the highway bridge near San Esteban / Los Andes.

rivers.davidBeta: Flowing down from the highest mountain in the Western Hemisphere (Aconcagua, 6,961m), the river cuts through a dramatic arid Andean gorge. Below the impassable railway chasm of Salto del Soldado, the river delivers pushy, fast Class IV big water with great wave trains and boulder rapids.

keyRapids.name: Soldier's Chute
keyRapids.description: Big waves and boiling seams between steep canyon walls.

hazards: Railway debris and old concrete chunks along banks
High-volume surges in warm weather
rivers.logistics: International highway Route 60 to Argentina. Easy vehicle shuttle.
rivers.pkrProTip: Stop by local vineyard estates in the Aconcagua valley for world-class Carménère after your run.
